channel.title: Smart.Market
channel.description: Daily market briefs and investing guides

item.title: 401(k) Basics: How to Capture Every Dollar of Your Employer Match
item.description: Learn how a 401(k) works, how employer match formulas and vesting really work, and how to set your contribution so you never leave free match money behind.

item.title: Asset Allocation by Age: Building a Portfolio That Fits Your Life
item.description: How to split your portfolio between stocks, bonds and cash at each stage of life, with age-based rules of thumb, a worked rebalancing example, and their limits.

item.title: Crypto in a Portfolio: Position Sizing Without Blowing Up
item.description: A risk-first guide to holding crypto: how to size a position you can afford to lose, set rebalancing rules, and avoid leverage, scams and concentration risk.

item.title: Dividend Investing: Building a Portfolio That Pays You
item.description: How dividend investing works: yield, payout ratio, dividend growth and yield on cost, with a 10-year worked example and the warning signs of an unsafe dividend.

item.title: Dollar-Cost Averaging vs. Lump Sum: What the Math Says
item.description: Should you invest a windfall all at once or spread it out? Worked examples show when a lump sum wins, when dollar-cost averaging helps, and how to decide.

item.title: How Big Should Your Emergency Fund Be?
item.description: Size your emergency fund in months of essential expenses, see a worked example, learn where to keep the cash and how to build it step by step without stress.

item.title: Fee-Only vs. Commission Financial Advisors: How to Choose
item.description: Learn how fee-only and commission financial advisors are paid, what fiduciary duty means, and how to check an advisor's record before you hire anyone.

item.title: How Much Do You Really Need to Retire? A Number-First Guide
item.description: Estimate your retirement number with the 4% rule: how it works, where it came from, its limits, and a worked example adjusted for pensions, CPP and Social Security.

item.title: How to Choose a Brokerage Account: A 7-Point Checklist
item.description: Compare brokerage accounts with a 7-point checklist covering SIPC and CIPF protection, fees, account types, fractional shares, research tools and support.

item.title: How to Invest Your First $1,000 (Without Regretting It)
item.description: A step-by-step plan for investing your first $1,000: what to do before you start, which account to use, what to buy, and the mistakes that cost beginners most.

item.title: How to Read an Earnings Report in 10 Minutes
item.description: A practical 10-minute routine for reading a quarterly earnings report: revenue, margins, EPS, cash flow, guidance and the red flags most investors miss.

item.title: How to Use a Stock Screener to Find Quality at a Fair Price
item.description: A beginner's guide to stock screeners: which filters matter, how to combine valuation, quality and risk, and how to research the shortlist a screen produces.

item.title: Index Funds Explained: Why Most Pros Can't Beat Them
item.description: What index funds are, how they work, why most actively managed funds trail them over time, and how to choose a low-cost index fund or ETF for your portfolio.

item.title: Inflation and Your Money: How to Protect Purchasing Power
item.description: Learn how inflation erodes purchasing power, see what $1,000 is worth after 20 years at 3% inflation, and explore practical ways to help your savings keep up.

item.title: Pay Down the Mortgage or Invest? The Math on Extra Payments
item.description: Should extra cash go to your mortgage or into investments? See a worked $400,000 example, the break-even return, and the non-math factors that matter.

item.title: P/E Ratio and Valuation Basics: What You're Really Paying For
item.description: Learn what the P/E ratio measures, how to calculate trailing and forward P/E, earnings yield and PEG, and why a low P/E is not automatically a bargain.

item.title: 15 Questions to Ask a Financial Advisor Before You Hire Them
item.description: Use these 15 questions to compare financial advisors on fees, fiduciary duty, credentials, conflicts and services before you sign an agreement or move money.

item.title: Roth IRA vs. Traditional IRA: Which One Fits You?
item.description: Roth or Traditional IRA? Compare tax timing, withdrawal rules and required distributions, see a worked example, and follow a simple decision tree to choose.

item.title: TFSA vs. RRSP: The Decision Tree for Canadians
item.description: TFSA or RRSP? Use this step-by-step decision tree, a worked tax example and plain-English rules to choose the right account for your next Canadian dollar.

item.title: The True Cost of a 1% Fee Over 30 Years
item.description: A 1% annual fee sounds small, but on $100,000 over 30 years it can cost about $176,000 versus a 0.05% fund. See the full table and how to cut your costs.

item.title: Reading the Yield Curve Like an Economist
item.description: What the Treasury yield curve shows, why it slopes, how to read spreads and implied forward rates, and what an inverted curve can and cannot tell you.
